courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Talent Management in the Hospitality Industry
courses.description: The course is aimed at introducing the concepts of talent management in hospitality industry. Topics may include talent management in overall HR planning; talent identification and development; and the related current practices in hospitality industry.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite: HTMG1010
courses.learning_outcomes:
After the course, students should acquire:
1) an overview of talent management in hospitality industry;
2) an understanding of the planning and implementation of talent development; and
3) an exposure to best practices in industry.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Innovation for Hospitality and Real Estate
courses.description:
Hospitality and Real Estate (HRE) are dynamic industries that need to constantly change to anticipate the evolving needs of guests, innovation therefore become an inseparable element that must be included in a business process to ensure the quality guest service delivery capability and the competitiveness of the industry. Even though our lives have changed in many ways with the fast development of technology and the evolved Industry 4.0. Innovation is not limited to tangible digital products like smart machine, robotic equipment or greener building, it also includes intangible management process, design or concepts that facilitate efficient use of human capital, marketing effectiveness and financial viability.

The objective of this course is to leverage industry expertise to facilitate discussion of tangible innovative products or intangible innovative process and system which are applicable to the Hospitality and Real Estate sectors, and assist students identify, evaluate and generate new business opportunities for HRE.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing this course, students should be able to

* Discuss the relationship of innovation and technology
* Understand how technology has disrupted the HRE industry
* Understand main characteristics of an innovation and identify its relevancy to the HRE
* Apply the learnt innovation concepts to a specific function/sector within the HRE industry
* Identify, evaluate and generate new business opportunities for HRE

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Essentials for Hospitality and Real Estate Projects
courses.description:
The use of (tactical) project management to deliver projects has been increasing in organizations.

A project can be defined as a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result.

Projects are particularly important for real estate and hospitality organizations, as a company’s strategic vision is operationalized through project management, with the transfer of projects to operations.

The ability successfully apply knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities has become an important management competency in the real estate and hospitality industries.

The objective of this course is to equip students with basic understanding of:
- project management concepts, including the project life cycle and the series of phases the project passes through from its start to its completion, and interdependencies.
- project management process groups (initiating, planning, executing, closing and monitoring & controlling).
- project management knowledge areas (integration, scope, schedule, cost, quality, resource, communications, risk, procurement, stakeholder).

In addition to discussing phases in a project, the students will be equipped with a beginner skills, and tool and techniques to understand typical hospitality project environments (new-build hotel, transition, renovation, product extension / upgrade, service upgrade, IT hard- and software implementation) and support general management and the project team in basic planning and executing of relevant project activities.

Finally, the course will explore how Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEFs) influence, constrain, or direct the project.
- Internal to the organization: e.g. culture, structure, and governance; geographic distribution of facilities and resources, infrastructure, resource availability, employee capability, etc.
- External to the organization: e.g. marketplace conditions, social and cultural influences and issues; legal restrictions, government or industry standards, physical environmental elements, etc.

Experiential learning activities such as real-world group projects from the real estate/hospitality fields, active case discussions, and business examples will be offered along with lectures for the purpose of enhancing students’ conceptual understanding and practical skills.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing this course, students should be able to

* understand a project life cycle and phases.
* understand the project management process groups.
* understand the project management knowledge areas.
* identify interdependencies.
* understand basic scope, schedule, cost and quality tools and techniques.
* understand key performance metrics for project success.
* describe how to manage stakeholder interests and relationships in each phase of the project life cycle.
* understand how Enterprise Environmental Factors facilitate (or hinder) successful project management.
* support effective project management teams.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Facilities Development and Management for Hospitality and Real Estate
courses.description: This course introduces the concepts, principles and process of facilities development and management from a hospitality facilities and real estate life cycle perspective, including inception and refinement of the development idea, the public roles of development approvals, the feasibility study, development planning, architectural design, construction and management. Furthermore, strategic and operational facilities management will be taught in the context of technology, cost, legal/contract, environment and performance management. Cases from both hospitality industry (e.g. hotels, museums, theme parks, transportation facilities) and real estate industry (e.g. office buildings, shopping malls, corporate real estate assets) will be discussed in the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: HTMG1010, HTMG3010 and HTMG3030
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
• Understand the concepts, principles and process of hospitality facilities/real estate development
• Adopt data from market research to develop and evaluate feasibility study report and development proposal
• Understand the major factors that affect hospitality facilities/real estate development and management; and
• Analyze and evaluate the hospitality facilities/real estate approaches and process

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Hospitality Strategic Management
courses.description: This course focuses on analysis, planning, change, and implementation issues associated with strategic management. It explores business missions, action plans, and evaluations of a hospitality organization. The emphases are on the value of analysing environments and formulating strategies linked to environmental conditions, and defending against organization weaknesses. Students learn how to engage in high-quality planning by examining situations from the perspectives of the customer, the employee, and management. Cases involving hospitality industry organizations are analysed extensively.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisites: HTMG1010, HTMG3010 and HTMG3030
courses.learning_outcomes:
1) Business Concepts and Functions
First, students are expected to understand three major theoretical perspectives on strategy formulation and implementation: a) the rational model that focuses on SWOT analysis, industry five-force analysis, and generic competitive strategies, b) the resource-based view of competitive advantage, and c) the stakeholder relationship perspective. Students will learn how to apply these theories to describe and prescribe strategies at both business- and corporate-levels. Second, students need to understand strategic management as a process and learn about the various approaches companies use to expand / diversify their businesses. Finally, students are expected to understand the notion of “fit” (external fit and internal fit) and its importance in strategy formulation and implementation (particularly in the area of designing organizational structures and control systems).

2) Analytical Skills
Business cases, video clips, and simulation exercises are used in this course for the purpose of training students’ analytical skills. Students are expected to apply different theoretical concepts and approaches to solve “real-world” problems. These exercises are also designed to help students understand that there are no “right” or “wrong” answers in strategy making. They need to deal with uncertainty, understand boundary conditions, and develop reasonable, realistic solutions.

3) Attitude / Values
The notion of ethical decision making is incorporated in every topic of this course. Students are required to learn not only the various ethical principles but also their implications in specific decision contexts. They will learn how to evaluate strategic proposals / solutions from different stakeholders’ perspectives and how to balance different interests / resolve conflicts. One significant element of this course is to encourage students to think beyond profits and take into account business ethics and social responsibilities in every strategic decision.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Hospitality & Real Estate Capstone Project
courses.description: The objectives of this course are: (1) to ensure that students are acquainted with actual hospitality and real estate working conditions, (2) to supplement theoretical and academic subject matter with practical experience, (3) to guide students in selecting permanent employment upon graduation, and (4) to nurture an academic mind and enable students to see the intimate relationship between theory and practice. There are two parts to this course: the internship where the students will engage in practicum experience in the hospitality and real estate industry, preferably during the summers before their graduation; the senior portfolio where the students will identify relevant industry issues and provide recommendations. These recommendations are grounded in literature and supported by empirical evidence. Students are also expected to conduct a project in their respective concentration areas.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: HTMG1010 and successful completion of the Summer Internship I and II.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Nurture an academic mind to learn from literature independently and make use of concepts to guide evidence based management.
2. Master tools to make concepts operational and tools to collect evidence to substantiate evidence based management.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Finance
courses.description:
The turmoil in real estate market, which is one of the largest and most important components of the financial system, could bring a negative impact to the world financial markets. The participants in the real estate market should understand how to evaluate the risk and return concerning various ways of financing. This course exposes students to concepts, theories and industry practice in real estate finance. Topics related to real estate finance, including legal foundation of real estate finance, mortgage loans, secondary mortgage market, mortgage-backed securities and financial leverage, will be discussed. Different alternative real estate financing vehicles, such as real estate investment trust (REIT), will also be examined.

The primary goal of this course is to help students develop the conceptual knowledge and analytical skills of real estate finance, including those related to the institutions and instruments used to finance residential and commercial real estate. After taking this course, the students are expected to understand the importance of different financing methods and be able to make informed real estate finance decisions.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:
• Understand the fundamental principles of real estate finance, the key concepts and the important relations underlying commercial real estate
• Demonstrate knowledge and understanding on how the mortgage loans are structured in real estate financing
• Apply different mortgage loans to commercial real estate projects
• Critically analyze the use of different financing methods in real estate projects

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Property Development and Investment
courses.description: This course provides fundamental knowledge of and analytical tools for property development and investment. It links space market and asset market in a dynamic real estate system and focuses on topics such as principles of commercial property investment analysis, cash flow analysis, real estate project investment analysis, etc. We will also discuss issues related to development project investment analysis, including definition and measurement of risk and return, excel modelling for real estate investment, feasibility studies, financial evaluation procedure based on net present value (NPV), and estimation of operational leverage and opportunity capital cost (OCC) for development investment. Global case studies will be used to guide theoretical learning and class discussion.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Global Real Estate Asset Management
courses.description: Real estate is largely known as an alternative investment in a portfolio. It is primarily viewed as return-enhancing and risk-reducing portfolio investments. It is thus important to understand the performance of real estate in an investment portfolio. This course provides theoretical foundation for real estate asset allocation with applications to private and public real estate investments globally. Topics include real estate as an alternative investment, private real estate investments, publicly traded real estate securities, private equity funds, different types of asset allocation, capital asset pricing model (CAPM) and modern portfolio theory (MPT). To take this course, students are required to have completed the relevant prerequisite courses in real estate finance and investment. After taking this course, students will be able to choose the best performance assets in the investment portfolio.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate; Pre-requisite: HTMG5001 and HTMG5002
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, the students should be able to:
• Understand the considerations of asset allocation for individual and institutional investors
• Determine the value of real estate securities
• Apply international CAPM and MPT in real estate asset allocation analysis
• Discuss basic strategic and tactical strategies of real estate portfolio
• Discuss basic features of real estate derivatives and their applications in investment portfolio

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Valuation
courses.description: This course introduces concepts and applications of valuation of real estate. Important concepts and techniques of real estate valuation will be covered to demonstrate how these can be applied to a range of property types or for a range of purposes. Topics related to real estate valuation will be covered including the economic forces driving the real estate value in the market, the needs for valuation, valuation methods and their applications, investment appraisal and development appraisal. After taking this course, the students are expected to have in-depth understanding of the concepts and techniques of valuation and demonstrate practical competence in undertaking different types of real estate valuation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:
• Understand the economic forces driving the real estate value
• Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the purposes for which valuations are undertaken
• Comprehend the concepts and techniques for undertaking real estate valuation of individual asset
• Apply the valuation principles and techniques through a group project

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Corporate Real Estate and Facilities Management
courses.description:
Corporate real estate strategies are the approaches organizations adopt to manage their property assets in ways to support their overall business objectives. Corporate real estate comprises the physical assets, such as offices, manufacturing plants, and retail facilities, that an organization owns or leases to support its business operations. These assets, while managed by the organization, may not be part of its core business. Rather, they function as essential infrastructure and facilities that enable the company to carry out its primary operations. Such strategies extend beyond the basic task of owning or leasing buildings. They involve aligning real estate decisions with the organization’s long-term vision, operational requirements, and financial goals.

This course introduces the fundamental knowledge and analytical frameworks of both Corporate Real Estate (CRE) – which focuses on a strategic level – and Facilities Management (FM) – which functions at an operational level. Students will learn how to establish strategic direction and ensure that the organization’s assets and facilities effectively support its business strategy. Effective facilities management not only benefits the organization itself, but also enhance the experience of its stakeholders, including staff, clients, and tenants.

This course is designed to facilitate students to:
1) develop a comprehensive understanding of the roles of CRE and FM within the real estate life cycle; 2) cultivate critical thinking skills across the various dimensions of FM; 3) acquire in-depth knowledge of facilities management at both strategic and operational levels.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc in Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:

* *Understand and articulate the role of Corporate Real Estate and Facilities Management profession in the overall competitive strategy of the organization in the context of when, where, what type and on what terms real estate services will be demanded*
* *Recognize the impact of the workplace on organizational productivity*
* *Assess the performance of real estate assets across a wide range of performance criteria with their knowledge of facilities management*
* *Apply the key competencies of a facility manager through problem solving and decision making in various business*

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Shopping Mall Development and Management
courses.description: Shopping mall is a dynamic business and has been one of the important assets in the investment portfolio. Unlike other real estate assets focusing only on the rental income paid by the tenants, the shopping mall predominantly concerns about the business of the tenants and how to increase their revenue. The shopping mall business thus requires thorough management to attract more customers and to increase the traffic flow. Despite the significance of site selection and financial feasibility, other important factors determining the success of a shopping mall include tenant mix, marketing and promotion, operation and maintenance, as well as asset enhancement. This course introduces theoretical knowledge and concepts affecting the development and management of the shopping mall. After taking this course, students should have a good understanding of the shopping mall business which allows them to work in the shopping mall development and management field.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc in Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:
• Describe the fundamental importance of shopping mall business in terms of development and management
• Apply theoretical framework to shopping mall business in Hong Kong
• Identify underperformed shopping mall and suggest its improvements
• Develop creative thinking, self-managed ability, team work spirit, analytical and communication skills through class discussion and project presentation

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Revitalisation of Historic Buildings
courses.description: Historic buildings bear witness to the development of a city and they are valuable and unique assets of urban community. In recent years, people have grown increasingly aware of the issue of the demolition and redevelopment of historic buildings. New generations are shouldering the responsibilities of inheriting and maintaining the culture of the city in a sustainable manner. This course focuses on historic buildings and sites in relations to their settings and aims to introduce the revitalisation theories, revitalisation policies and revitalisation process. Case studies are used to illustrate revitalisation projects in Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland, Macau and Singapore.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc in Real Estate

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Economics
courses.description: Real estate, governing one-third of the world’s assets, plays an important role in the capital markets. It is thus crucial to understand how the real estate system works and what economic forces drive the real estate value. In the real estate system, there are two markets (space market and asset market) and one industry (development industry). Space market is essential to the overall real estate system as it governs rents. Changes in rent promptly influence the demand for real estate asset market, and development industry at a later date. This course introduces urban and real estate economics. Urban economics is the primary branch of economics for studying the space market. Topics related to urban economics and real estate space-market analysis will be covered, including four-quadrant model, central place theory, residual theory of land value, the concept of rent, bid-rent analysis, neighborhood life cycle, property life cycle, and demand and supply for real estate space market. After taking this course, students are expected to have in-depth understanding of factors that trigger the functioning of real estate space markets.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:
• Understand the theories and principles of urban economics that are of paramount importance in making well-informed real estate investment decisions
• Comprehend the economic principles and concepts that determine the land value and rent in the city
• Apply the principles of land value and rent determinants in conducting the real estate market analysis
• Analyze Hong Kong’s and Mainland China’s real estate space markets

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Capstone Research Project
courses.description: The objectives of this course are: (1) to supplement the study of theoretical perspectives with empirical research evidence, (2) to guide students in conducting empirical research, and (3) to nurture an academic mind and enable students to study the intimate relationship between theory and practice. Students will identify relevant industry issues and provide policy recommendations. These recommendations are grounded in academic literature and supported by empirical evidence. Students are expected to conduct a behavioral research project on an issue related to the hospitality and real estate industry.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc in Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Nurture an academic mind to learn from literature independently and make use of concepts to guide evidence based management
2. Master tools to make concepts operational and tools to collect evidence to substantiate evidence based management
3. Our students will demonstrate an understanding of concepts, theories, and practices pertaining to strategic management of hospitality and real estate (HRE) businesses
4. Our students will apply critical thinking and problem solving skills relevant to strategically managing HRE business
5. Our students will demonstrate effective communication, teamwork and leadership skills applicable to a HRE setting

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Financial Reporting and Analysis
courses.description: Real estate entities that construct, manage and hold real properties encounter various financial reporting issues that could affect their performance measurement. In real estate industry, the financial reporting is in fact unique and complex. While the industry has its own specific standards, it is mandatory that these entities also need to follow the statutory reporting requirements. This course covers the financial reporting practices adopted in the real estate industry and applies the financial statement analysis techniques in the performance measurement and valuation of real estate entities. Topics include fundamental accounting techniques and practices, relevant financial reporting standards for the real estate industry, subsequent measurement of investment property, as well as real estate financing and tax considerations. After taking this course, students are expected to have an in-depth understanding of the financial reporting standards required and be able to apply these standards in the valuation of real estate entities.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, the students should be able to:
• Understand the principles of financial reporting required in the real estate industry
• Assess the subsequent measurement of investment property
• Comprehend the real estate financing and tax considerations
• Apply the principles of financial reporting in conducting the analysis of real estate companies
• Analyze the financial reporting of the real estate companies in Hong Kong and globally

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Selected Topics in Real Estate
courses.description: This course is designed to investigate and to discuss selected topics of current interests in the area of real estate.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes: After completion of the course, student should be able to gain the latest perspective on different real estate issues and topics.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Field Study
courses.description: Experiential learning is a crucial element of real estate study. Since the real estate industry involves complex work practices and diverse professional fields, it is necessary for students to learn first-hand knowledge of real estate planning, development, management, and investment through site visits and field trips, local or overseas. This course is designed to extend students’ real estate learning beyond the classroom. The course combines classroom lectures / workshops on chosen real estate topics with a field trip to a location typically outside Hong Kong. Students are expected to apply theoretical concepts and tools to analyze real-world cases, conduct market research, and/or solve problems in a specific real estate area. The topics of this course will vary depending on different instructors, field trip locations, and project tasks.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: PropTech: Emerging Trends and Opportunities
courses.description: The real estate industry, which accounts for a significant portion of global capital assets, used to be known for relying on traditional practices and lacking capacity for continuous innovation. This, however, has changed in recent years with the fast development of property technology (PropTech) applications. PropTech refers to a wide range of technology-enabled solutions used to optimize all stages of the real estate process, from property design, construction, management to property buying, leasing, and selling. This course helps students understand how the Internet, mobile and digital technologies have changed residential and commercial real estate business operations. Students will learn to compare and evaluate PropTech solutions and understand the business opportunities and potential challenges associated with these new tools/platforms. Real-world cases and examples will be used to discuss the impact of PropTech on real estate practices.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Real Estate

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Real Estate Securitization
courses.description: This applied course utilizes advanced data analytics and AI models to understand securitized real estate asset markets, including their structural risks. The curriculum advances fixed-income and credit risk analysis through specialized study of residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities (MBS/CMBS), extending to diverse real estate-backed securities. Students gain practical experience with cutting-edge big data, AI models and analytical tools central to modern real estate securitization markets. Coursework emphasizes hands-on Big Data analytics for processing extensive loan-level datasets, Monte Carlo simulation, options-based valuation, and risk management approaches in loan pooling, tranching, and rating processes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

1. **Understand securitization fundamentals**: Comprehend the unique features of asset-backed securities and the economic rationale for securitization in real estate markets
2. **Apply advanced valuation techniques**: Utilize options-based models to value mortgage-backed securities and structured products
3. **Master big data analytics**: Process and analyze extensive loan-level datasets using modern data analytics tools
4. **Evaluate credit risk**: Apply empirical hazard models and competing risk frameworks to assess prepayment and default behavior
5. **Analyze market structures**: Understand the mechanics of TBA markets, repo agreements, and credit risk transfer mechanisms
6. **Assess rating methodologies**: Evaluate how rating agencies approach structured products and understand stress-testing techniques

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Leadership and Change Management in Experience Economy
courses.description: The rapidly evolving experience economy requires future leaders to develop systemic thinking about what their organizations can offer to customers, employees, and other stakeholders, as well as how their businesses can positively impact society. Leadership in the experience economy entails the ability to address key challenges specific to experience-driven industries, such as motivating, engaging, and empowering employees; effectively leading team collaboration; initiating and managing organizational change; managing crisis; fostering innovation, to name just a few. This course examines the interplay between leadership, creativity, team dynamics, and organizational change within the context of the experience economy. It connects real-world cases and scenarios of leadership challenges in the experience economy with discussions of recent research on leadership and organizational change management.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of contemporary leadership theories, practices, and challenges within the context of the experience economy.
2. Apply leadership competencies, including motivating and empowering teams, fostering creativity, and managing changes, to address real-world challenges in experience-driven businesses.
3. Analyze and design effective strategies for initiating, implementing, and sustaining organizational change, considering the complexities of the experience economy.
4. Demonstrate critical thinking and problem-solving skills relevant to experience-driven businesses.
5. Develop and demonstrate collaboration skills in teamwork.
6. Cultivate a mindset that prioritizes ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and systemic thinking to enhance the positive impact of leadership practices on customers, employees, and other stakeholders in the experience economy.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Finance and Investment in Experience Industries
courses.description: Interest in the experience economy has surged in recent years, covering sectors such as entertainment, tourism, hospitality, and events. The core business model of these industries often involves significant investments in real property, facilities, and infrastructure to generate sustainable returns. This course introduces students to the financial and investment principles underlying the experience industries. It equips students with the knowledge and tools to evaluate financial performance, assess investment opportunities, and manage risk and return in this dynamic sector. Students will learn to build cash flow models, perform investment appraisals, and analyze financing decisions, enabling them to advise businesses on strategic investment choices. The course emphasizes practical application of financial analysis and investment strategy, blending academic theory with real-world case studies from hospitality, tourism, and event enterprises.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand and apply financial management principles within the experience industries.
2. Construct and analyze cash flows and financial models for projects in tourism, hospitality, entertainment, vents and other experience industries.
3. Evaluate investment returns, cost of capital, and risks specific to experience industry contexts.
4. Formulate financing strategies and assess funding sources for industry projects.
5. Communicate financial insights effectively in professional contexts.
6. Demonstrate ethical awareness in financial and investment decision-making.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Hospitality Asset Valuation and Management
courses.description: The hospitality sector encompasses a wide range of industry segments that are closely tied to the daily experience of all members of the society. These industries are typically experience-oriented such as lodging, food and beverages, tourism, sports, event planning and exhibitions, to name just a few. At the same time, engaging in these services requires considerable capital investment in the provision of hardware: hotels, bars and restaurants, exhibition and convention centres, theme parks, golf courses, clubs and gaming facilities etc. They are part and parcel to the success of an experience economy. This course focuses on the valuation and management of hospitality-related asset portfolios. Asset valuation is an integral part of business operations as it facilitates the financing, taxation, statutory reporting and market transaction of assets. It is a good performance yardstick to measure certain aspects of business success and viability. Meanwhile, portfolio asset management is a key skill that can contribute to asset value growth. Superior management and optimal capital structures can greatly enhance portfolio values and returns to investment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Digital Transformation in Experience Economy
courses.description: In an increasingly digital and experience-rich world, the ability to transform and adapt to new technologies is crucial for businesses to survive and thrive. This course focuses on the intersection of digital transformation and the experience economy, where companies’ effectiveness in improving customer experiences is at the forefront of value creation. Students will explore the key principles and strategies for successfully navigating digital transformation in the unique landscape of the experience economy. They will learn to identify opportunities for leveraging digital technologies to create memorable and valuable customer experiences. Topics covered include but are not limited to understanding the experience economy and its impact on business operations; the role of digital technologies in creating and enhancing customer experiences; strategies for building organizational capabilities in implementing digital transformation initiatives; emerging technologies and their potential applications in the experience economy, such as AI, IoT, and other immersive technologies; and measuring the success of digital transformation efforts and their impact on customer experience and business performance. By the end of the course, students will be well-prepared to contribute to the digital transformation journeys of businesses and to help shape the future of the experience economy.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
CLO 1: *Utilize tools and frameworks to specify and align company objectives with the digital transformation landscape.*

CLO 2: *Analyze and build customer experiences to maximize digital transformation efficiency and effectiveness.*

CLO 3: *Analyze and understand external market factors and consumer psychology relating to customer experience and digital transformation trends and preferences.*

CLO 4: *Develop and deliver effective narratives and communications to convey the digital transformation means and ends to customers and CMOs.*

CLO 5: *Develop effective teamwork and leadership skills.*

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Experience Innovation
courses.description: In an era where exceptional service experiences are paramount, this course explores how organizations can transform their service offerings through innovative practices and technologies. Students will learn to shift from traditional product-centric approaches to dynamic, service-centric models that prioritize customer satisfaction and loyalty. The course integrates insights from diverse fields such as psychology and behavioral economics, providing a rich theoretical foundation for understanding and influencing consumer behavior. Students will delve into cutting-edge innovations, including automation, artificial intelligence (AI), and immersive realities (AR/VR), examining their potential to enhance service delivery and create memorable customer interactions. Through a semester-long project and critical analysis of modern business cases, students will develop strategies to design, prototype, and validate technologically-infused service experiences, ultimately learning how to foster a culture of innovation and position their organizations as leaders in a competitive marketplace.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy; or MBA Technology and Innovation
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Analyze the shift from product-centric to service-dominant logic in the modern economy.
* Apply principles from psychology and behavioral economics to diagnose and predict customer behavior within service systems.
* Evaluate the strategic application of emerging technologies for enhancing customer experiences.
* Master a structured innovation process to move from complex customer problems to viable, tech-driven solutions.
* Develop and test service prototypes that effectively integrate digital and physical touchpoints.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: HR Analytics Mastery in Hospitality
courses.description:
In today's evolving business landscape, the hospitality industry faces unique challenges such as talent shortages, technological advancements, evolving guest expectations, and supply chain disruptions. These challenges necessitate innovative solutions to maintain competitiveness and ensure operational efficiency. HR analytics is a key solution in this context.
HR analytics is essential in the hospitality industry for several reasons. It optimizes workforce performance by identifying performance trends, training needs, and areas for improvement. This ensures that employees are well-equipped to meet customer expectations, which is crucial in a customer-centric industry like hospitality.
This course covers HR analytics concepts specific to the hospitality industry, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics, HR lifecycle metrics, training, rewards, and basic statistical methods. Key topics include HR metrics and KPIs, data collection and management, employee lifecycle analytics, diversity and inclusion, strategic workforce planning, and ethical considerations in HR analytics. Students will engage in hands-on projects and case studies specific to the hospitality industry, applying analytical techniques to real-world HR challenges that hotels, restaurants, and other hospitality businesses.
By the end of this course, students will be equipped to drive impactful HR strategies within their organizations, leveraging data analytics to deliver superior outcomes. This course seeks to enhance students' analytical skills and make data-driven decisions in the hospitality sector.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Critically analyze complex HR datasets from the hospitality industry to identify trends, correlations, and performance gaps using descriptive analytics techniques.
2. Apply and integrate predictive and prescriptive analytics models to forecast workforce needs and recommend evidence-based HR strategies for hospitality operations.
3. Design and implement data-driven HR dashboards and KPI frameworks that support strategic workforce planning and operational decision-making in hospitality organizations.
4. Evaluate ethical considerations, diversity, and inclusion principles in the application of HR analytics, demonstrating sound judgment in decision-making and policy development.
5. Communicate and justify analytical insights and predictive models to stakeholders through data visualization and storytelling, influencing strategic HR decisions in hospitality businesses.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Hospitality Business Reporting and Analysis
courses.description: Hospitality business entities encounter various reporting issues that affect their performance measurement. In the hospitality and tourism industry, business entities follow specific industry key performance indicators in financial reporting. Moreover, sustainability and ESG reporting bears particular significance. This course covers the financial reporting practices adopted by the hospitality industry and applies the financial statement analysis techniques in the performance measurement and valuation of these entities. In addition, the course analyses entities across the ESG reporting framework and evaluates their sustainability performances. After taking this course, students are expected to have an in-depth understanding of the financial and ESG reporting standards required and to be able to apply these standards in the performance evaluation of hospitality business entities.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the principles of financial reporting required for hospitality entities.
2. Assess the reporting and specific measurement of revenue, expenses, and property-related assets, including hotel property, plant & equipment, and intangible assets possessed by hospitality businesses.
3. Comprehend sustainability and ESG reporting for hospitality entities.
4. Apply the principles of financial and sustainability reporting to conduct analysis for hospitality entities.
5. Analyze the performance of hospitality entities in Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland, and globally.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Design Thinking and Business Model Innovation in Experience Economy
courses.description:
Design Thinking is a process for creatively and systematically solving problems by prioritizing people and their needs. It emphasizes a deep understanding of user experiences and employs empathetic, iterative, and non-linear processes for imagination and idea generation. In this course, students will learn the fundamental principles and tools of design thinking and apply them to practical projects aimed at incorporating human-centred design into business model innovation within experience industries.

Students will be guided through the processes of understanding customer needs, building empathy with customers, identifying problems, collecting and analysing data, generating solutions, and testing those solutions. By doing so, they are expected to develop a deeper understanding of how to generate creative business ideas and implement them within well-designed business models. These models will involve detailed considerations such as competitor analysis, value proposition, cost and revenue analysis, activity design, and partnership formation. By exploring the intersection of design thinking and business model innovation in the context of experience-driven industries—such as hospitality, tourism, events, healthcare, sports, and retail—students will develop skills in strategic thinking, creative problem-solving, team collaboration, communication, and storytelling. Through a combination of lectures, creativity exercises, games, and hands-on problem-solving challenges, this course equips students with the tools to address complex challenges and drive innovation in dynamic, experience-based markets.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand and apply fundamental design thinking processes and tools.
2. Understand key concepts, theories, and analytical frameworks related to business model innovation in the experience economy.
3. Demonstrate ability to translate broadly defined opportunities into actionable business model solutions for experience-driven organizations.
4. Demonstrate ability to identify customer/employee needs, generate creative ideas, and develop innovative solutions for real-world business problems.
5. Develop teamwork skills in design-based problem solving.
6. Understand and apply ethical principles in research, design, and business model building.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Current Issues in Global Tourism, Hospitality, and Events
courses.description: This graduate-level seminar provides an in-depth examination of emerging trends and critical challenges in global tourism, hospitality, and events. Students will explore contemporary and pressing issues in the dynamic and evolving landscape of the global tourism, hospitality, event, and related industries. Through case studies, discussions, guest speeches by industry leaders, and field trips, students will critically assess how these trends shape the future of the field and formulate strategic responses to address emerging challenges. Through an interdisciplinary lens, this course is designed to cultivate critical thinking, analytical reasoning, strategic decision-making, and a global perspective.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Critically identify and evaluate emerging trends and challenges in the global tourism, hospitality, and event industries using interdisciplinary frameworks.
* Examine the implications of contemporary issues on industry growth and their impact on broader societal development.
* Formulate effective strategies to address challenges and capitalize on opportunities within these industries.
* Demonstrate a global/cross-cultural perspective, showcase critical thinking and analytical skills to evaluate emerging industry trends from a global standpoint.
* Utilize theoretical concepts in practical contexts through effective communication, research, and problem-solving skills.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: ESG in Action: Learn from Experience Industry Practices
courses.description: This course explores Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices within the context of experience industries such as hospitality, tourism, events, healthcare, creative industries, and retail. Designed for master-level students, the course combines theoretical foundations with practical insights delivered by industry executives and faculty members. Students will analyse ESG challenges and real-world practices, culminating in a group project where they propose actionable ESG solutions for partner organizations. The course provides students with the conceptual tools and applied skills needed to integrate ESG principles into business strategies for the experience industries.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles and their relevance to experience-driven industries.
2. Critically evaluate the ESG challenges and opportunities faced by businesses in the experience industries, including sustainability, stakeholder engagement, and governance practices.
3. Apply theoretical knowledge and industry insights to identify areas for improvement in a partner company’s ESG practices and propose feasible, innovative, and actionable solutions tailored to the organization’s specific challenges.
4. Enhance teamwork, leadership, and project management skills by collaborating in diverse groups to deliver a well-researched and impactful ESG project.
5. Strengthen communication and professional skills by interacting with industry professionals in the project process.
6. Demonstrate abilities to make ethical business decisions.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Experience Design and Management in Action: Learn from Industry Practices
courses.description: This course provides students with an in-depth understanding of experience design and management practices in the context of experience industries. Students will explore the frameworks, tools, real-world issues and solutions behind designing and managing meaningful experiences for customers, users, and employees. With a focus on identifying and addressing pain points, students will learn to create innovative and sustainable solutions that enhance satisfaction, loyalty, and overall experience quality. Featuring industry guest lectures and problem-solving tasks / projects, the course bridges academic knowledge with practical insights to prepare students for dynamic challenges in the field.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy; or MSc Real Estate
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of fundamental principles, frameworks, and tools for designing and managing customer and employee experiences in the context of experience industries.
2. Critically evaluate current customer and employee experience challenges, pain points, and opportunities faced by businesses in the experience economy, using real-world case studies and industry insights.
3. Demonstrate abilities to generate creative and feasible solutions to improve experience design and management practices.
4. Strengthen teamwork, leadership, and project management skills by working collaboratively in diverse groups to deliver a comprehensive and well-researched experience design project.
5. Demonstrate abilities to make ethical decisions related to experience design and management.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Field Study on the Experience Economy
courses.description: This field study course offers students an immersive learning experience in the global experience economy. The course combines academic inquiry with experiential learning, enabling students to observe, analyze, compare, and evaluate business practices in experience design, investment, and management across diverse industries and geographical contexts. Working in teams, students will conduct a project addressing a real-world business challenge, applying theoretical frameworks to develop practical and culturally informed policy recommendations or business solutions. Through site visits, field observations, and intercultural collaboration, students will gain deeper insights into the current practices, issues, challenges, and opportunities facing organizations operating in various experience-driven industries.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Gain an in-depth understanding of business practices in the experience-driven industries.
* Compare and evaluate experience design and management issues / practices across different cultural contexts.
* Synthesize insights from company visits, cultural immersion, and academic interactions to formulate actionable recommendations for industry practitioners.
* Improve research and problem-solving skills.
* Collaborate effectively in cross-cultural teams to investigate business challenges and develop solutions for enhancing experience.
* Reflect critically on the influence of cultural and contextual factors on experience and managerial decision-making in global markets.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Aviation Experience Management
courses.description:
Effective management of service experiences in aviation not only enhances customer satisfaction but also drives operational efficiency and fosters brand loyalty. Modern aviation services encompass a diverse range of interactions, from check-in and boarding to in-flight experiences. This course is designed to explore the principles of designing, delivering, and managing exceptional service experiences within the aviation industry. It aims to equip students with the knowledge and critical skills needed to optimize customer interactions and ensure a seamless, end-to-end journey.

Key topics include:
• Marketing strategies in aviation.
• Service design and innovation.
• Customer relationship management.
• Quality assurance in service delivery.

The course emphasizes strategies to create a holistic, memorable customer experience, ensuring passengers feel valued at every step of their journey.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Aviation Management; or MSc Leadership for Experience Economy
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Understand the key principles of marketing and how they apply to the aviation industry.
* Analyze consumer behavior in air travel and the factors influencing passenger satisfaction.
* Evaluate airline branding, positioning, and customer engagement strategies.
* Examine loyalty programs and CRM (Customer Relationship Management) in aviation.
* Apply marketing theories to real-world airline cases and develop recommendations for improving customer experience.

courses.subject: HTMG
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: To monitor students' progress in thesis and research.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Business Administration
courses.learning_outcomes: The goal of this course is to monitor students’ progress in thesis and research. Upon completing this course, students will develop a skill to summarize the essential ingredients of a paper in a concise way, to develop an original research topic, and to empirically execute the idea using what they have learned in other seminar courses.
